Judged against the repository's own normative design documents (`docs/specs/architecture-v1.md`,
`docs/specs/spec-draft-v3.md`), not against generic C# style.

## Executive summary

This is a well-architected codebase with a disciplined core — strict downward layering, explicit AOT-safe dispatch tables, atomic writes with an fsync'd write-ahead journal, and a frozen-format register that the code visibly respects. The problems are not architectural drift; they are three narrower structural weaknesses that the design's own strengths have made easy to miss.

The most expensive one is that failures are routinely converted into successes at the boundary between a subsystem and the user. The pattern repeats independently in six places: a post-commit source disposition that fails (locked file, full archive, a rejected Recycle Bin call) is written to the journal and the job log and then returned as `JobOutcome.Succeeded` with a null Error, so the activity row is green and the status bar's LastError is cleared; a deletion whose audit-append fails destroys the file and loses the only record of it, and still reports success; directories the scanner cannot open are downgraded from Fatal to Warning and then logged and discarded by both the dry-run engine and the manual-run handler, so the user approves a `PermanentDelete` run against a plan that silently covered a partial tree; a failed catalog reload after a profile save or delete is logged at warning level and reported as OK, leaving the engine executing the stale profile — including a stale `OnSuccessAction`; a settings load that fails leaves the Settings dialog fully populated with constructor defaults, and the next Save persists those defaults over the real settings.json, resetting a relocated `ProfilesDirectory` and making the user's entire profile list vanish; and an unparseable settings.json is replaced by defaults with the original bytes left to be overwritten by that same next save. Individually each is a few lines. Collectively they mean the product's safety story — dry run first, then dispose of sources — has holes precisely at the points where the user is being asked to trust it. Every one of these is fixable without touching a frozen format: `EngineWarningEvent` already exists on the wire and is already routed to the UI's notice bar.

The second weakness is that the compiler-invisible coupling the repo depends on is only partly guarded. The register documents three hand-maintained parallel tables; `IpcRequestTypesTests` pins one leg of one of them. The unguarded leg has already drifted: the flagship end-to-end test hand-rebuilds the DI graph under a comment claiming parity with Program.cs and registers 14 handlers where production registers 17 — missing `DryRunStreamHandler`, which is the handler the UI uses for *every* dry run. Program.cs itself lists all 17 handler types twice by hand. In the UI, three row types share five command names that are bound by reflection inside `x:CompileBindings="False"` regions, held in step by nothing but a comment on each type. None of these produce a compile error when they break; they produce a NOT_IMPLEMENTED response or a dead right-click menu item.

The third is that one capability is implemented twice and the copies have already diverged in ways that matter. `AtomicPlacer` and `CrashRecovery` both implement the staged-overwrite `File.Replace` → two-step-move fallback; the placer's copy guards the fallback with `File.Exists(finalPath)` and documents that idempotency as mandatory, and the recovery copy — the one that replays the same journal rows on every service start — omits the guard, so a recovery pass interrupted between the two moves strands the final name absent forever. `DryRunEngine` carries a complete batched simulation pipeline alongside the streamed one that the UI actually uses, and the memory bound added to the streamed sweep was never applied to the batched half. `DryRunSourcesTab` and `DryRunDestinationsTab` are ~390 byte-identical lines of the same tab mechanism written twice, in the file that carries 42 of the repo's 128 commits — a memory-leak fix and a parallelization change were each demonstrably applied twice in a single diff.

The shape of the fix is: first close the silent-success holes and the dead code (small, reversible, each verified by one new test); then add the guards that convert runtime-silent coupling into compile errors or red tests; then, and only with characterization tests and benchmarks in place, consolidate the two genuinely duplicated implementations.

Scope honesty: this review covered `src/`, `tests/` and `benchmarks/` by reading and searching only — nothing was built, run, or profiled. `third_party/TreeDataGrid` and the PowerShell integration harnesses were treated as frozen and not assessed. Four areas could be assessed only by reading because they have no tests at all and, in three cases, cannot be constructed by a test: `EngineHost`'s startup ordering (the I-RECOVER-FIRST invariant), the service composition root, `IpcGateway`'s reconnect and poison-recycle rules, and `ScanScheduler`'s worker pool lifecycle. Confidence in those four is correspondingly lower, and the roadmap treats making them testable as work in its own right rather than assuming they are correct.

### Themes

**Failures silently reported as success at the user boundary** — 6 findings: settings-save-after-failed-load-overwrites-real-settings, disposition-and-audit-failures-reported-as-clean-success, enumeration-warnings-dropped-from-dry-run-and-manual-run, catalog-reload-failure-three-semantics, startup-catalog-load-failure-serves-empty-profile-list, corrupt-settings-file-silently-replaced-by-defaults

The dominant cost in the repo. Six independent code paths convert a real failure into a clean success or a silent empty result: post-commit disposition failure returns JobOutcome.Succeeded with a null Error and clears LastError; a failed deletion-audit append still reports the delete as clean; enumeration faults are downgraded to warnings and then dropped by both dry-run and manual-run consumers, so the plan the user approves claims a complete tree; a failed catalog reload after save/delete reports OK while the engine keeps executing the stale profile; a failed settings load leaves the dialog on constructor defaults that the next Save writes over the user's real settings.json; an unparseable settings.json is replaced by defaults with no copy kept. The common root is that these subsystems have a logging channel but no result channel back to the caller, even though EngineWarningEvent already exists on the wire and is already routed to the UI notice bar. Two of these can lose user data outright (a relocated ProfilesDirectory reset; a PermanentDelete run approved against a partial plan).

**Compiler-invisible coupling that nothing guards, and has already drifted** — 6 findings: service-composition-root-untestable-and-drifted, ipc-handler-list-written-twice, handler-registration-listed-twice-in-composition-root, dryrun-row-commands-no-shared-contract, dry-run-row-command-block, destination-row-kind-vocabulary-restated

The architecture deliberately trades reflection for hand-maintained tables (AOT constraint) and deliberately opts four XAML regions out of compiled bindings. Both are sound choices, but only one leg of one table is pinned by a test. The consequences are already visible: the end-to-end smoke test's hand-rebuilt DI graph is missing three handlers including the one the UI uses for every dry run; Program.cs lists all 17 handlers twice with nothing linking the lists; three dry-run row types share five reflection-bound command names held together by a comment; and the destination-kind key/icon/brush vocabulary is restated in seven places where a mismatch renders a blank glyph or a chip that filters nothing. Every failure in this theme is runtime-silent. The fix is uniformly cheap — a marker interface, DI enumeration of explicit registrations, one key-set assertion — and converts each into a build error or a red test.

**One capability implemented twice, with the copies already diverged** — 5 findings: staged-replace-fallback-duplicated, batched-dryrun-sweep-unbounded, batched-dry-run-pipeline-has-no-production-client, dryrun-tabs-one-class-written-twice, dry-run-tab-parallel-lifecycle

Three cases, ordered by damage. (1) The staged-overwrite replace primitive exists in AtomicPlacer and again in CrashRecovery; the placer's fallback is idempotent by explicit design and the recovery copy is not, which is a latent data-stranding bug on the single most safety-critical write in the product. (2) DryRunEngine maintains a complete batched pipeline beside the streamed one; only the streamed half has a production client, and the sweep memory bound added to it was never applied to the batched half. (3) DryRunSourcesTab and DryRunDestinationsTab are ~390 byte-identical lines of one tab mechanism, in the file carrying 33% of all commits — a leak fix and a parallelization change were each applied twice in one diff. The root is the same in all three: no shared abstraction was introduced when a second caller appeared, so hardening lands on whichever copy the author was looking at.

**The service's startup and transport layers cannot be constructed by a test** — 6 findings: enginehost-startup-sequence-unreachable, service-composition-root-untestable-and-drifted, ipcgateway-no-coverage-static-transport, scanscheduler-worker-lifecycle-unobservable, cron-parser-zero-tests, storagebar-band-layout-inside-render

EngineHost is internal in an assembly with no InternalsVisibleTo, so the I-RECOVER-FIRST ordering — crash recovery must complete before the IPC server accepts connections, bridges must be installed after catalog.Reload() and before the orchestrator starts — is asserted nowhere, even though CrashRecovery itself has 1085 lines of tests. The DI graph lives inline in Program.Main and is likewise unbuildable, which is why the smoke test's hand-copy drifted. IpcGateway acquires connections through static ServiceLauncher/IpcClient calls over a sealed private-constructor type, so its poison-recycle and error-code drop rules — the entire service-restart recovery story — have no test file. ScanScheduler's process-wide OS-thread ceiling is a private int behind a 15-second private const. These are not defects; they are the reason a defect in any of them would be invisible, and they gate the structural work in Tier 3.

**Static and default-valued seams that quietly defeat injection** — 3 findings: settings-static-defaults-override-injected-enginepaths, sourcescanner-optional-volume-port, runprofile-detached-scan-escapes-host-lifetime

The engine has a clean injectable EnginePaths root, but the two directories that hold user data escape it: GlobalSettings.ProfilesDirectory and .ScratchDirectory fall back to process-global statics, and SettingsService returns those without rebasing on the injected paths — so the end-to-end test needs a hand-written pin (with a comment explaining why) for profiles, and has none at all for scratch, meaning a spilling dry run in the test suite writes into the developer's real %LOCALAPPDATA%. Similarly SourceScanner's IVolumeInfoProvider is an optional parameter whose null branch collapses every path to one synthetic volume, so the per-volume thread-budget routing that ScanScheduler exists to implement is a production-only code path that no test or benchmark exercises. RunProfileHandler's detached Task.Run with CancellationToken.None is the same shape: work with no owner and no observable lifetime.

**Accreted dead code, concentrated in the hottest file** — 4 findings: dead-dryrun-row-computed-props, dead-existing-stats-counter, dead-file-dryrun-spool-factory, dead-unittest1-scaffolding

Low cost individually, but notable for where it sits: ten computed properties on the dry-run row records with no binding and no caller (including HasDestructiveAction, one character from the real HasDestructiveActions, in a file with reflection-bound regions), a telemetry counter that is never incremented so both completion logs permanently report '0 existing-target stats', an unreferenced spool factory that is a second construction path for a persisted snapshot format, and two dotnet-new scaffolding tests. All four are compiler-verified or grep-verified deletions.

**Shell view model absorbing workflow implementation** — 1 finding: mainwindow-vm-shell-plus-six-workflows

Lowest-cost theme, included because it explains an asymmetry rather than a size problem. MainWindowViewModel legitimately owns cross-view-model routing, but the profile-import workflow does raw File.OpenRead + JsonSerializer.Deserialize inline while the symmetric export routes through a dedicated Services/ProfileExport helper whose own doc says exported files must round-trip back through Import. There is no ProfileImport counterpart, so the two halves of a documented interchange format have no single place to check, and the safety invariant that imports arrive Active = false is an inline `with` expression reachable only through a folder-picker fake.

## Constraints — read before changing anything

The implementing agent must treat everything in this section as immovable unless the task is
explicitly a format migration. Renaming a member listed here does not break the build — it breaks
user data already on disk, or the wire compatibility between two separately-shipped executables.

### Frozen types (39)

*Serialized to disk or across the process boundary. Member names are the format.*

#### `FileManager.Contracts.Profiles.Profile (and its entire graph: TriggerSettings, ScheduleSettings, SourceConfig, TransformerStep, TargetConfig, PolicySettings, FilterSet, AttributeFilterSettings, LoggingSettings)`

Persisted as profiles/*.json on user machines and re-read on every service start. Property NAMES are the JSON keys; the record is round-tripped through System.Text.Json source-gen. Any profile written by an older build must still load, so EVERY type reachable from Profile is frozen: no renaming members, no splitting/merging records, no moving a member to a nested type. Profile.Id is additionally aliased to the wire name "ProfileId" and the file NAME is the Guid.

*Mechanism:* serialization

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Contracts/Profiles/Profile.cs:18; src/FileManager.Contracts/FileManagerJsonContext.cs:13; src/FileManager.Core/Profiles/ProfileStore.cs:130; tests/FileManager.Scripts.Windows.Tests/mirror/profiles/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222.json:3

#### `All Profile enums: SyncMode, TargetLayout, ConflictResolution, OverwriteHandling, VerificationMethod, OnSuccessAction, OnFailureAction, MetadataOnConflict, ArgumentMode, OutputMode, MissedRunPolicy, LogVerbosity`

Serialized BY NAME into profiles/*.json and over IPC (UseStringEnumConverter). Renaming a member silently invalidates every stored profile. VerificationMethod additionally pins wire names via [JsonStringEnumMemberName("XXH3-128"/"SHA256")] AND its declaration ORDER is a wire contract because journal records serialize enums as integers.

*Mechanism:* serialization

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Contracts/FileManagerJsonContext.cs:12; src/FileManager.Contracts/Profiles/Profile.cs:168; src/FileManager.Contracts/Profiles/Profile.cs:175

#### `FileManager.Contracts.IPC.IpcRequest and all 18 derived records (GetStatusRequest … ShutdownRequest)`

Polymorphic wire format with a "type" discriminator table. The discriminator strings are duplicated in three places that must agree: the [JsonDerivedType] attributes, IpcRequestTypes' const table + DiscriminatorOf switch, and each handler's RequestType property used as the DI dispatch-table key. Deleting/renaming a derived record or changing a discriminator breaks UI↔service compatibility at runtime (NOT_IMPLEMENTED / IPC_MALFORMED), not at compile time.

*Mechanism:* serialization

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IpcRequest.cs:8; src/FileManager.Core/IPC/IpcRequestTypes.cs:10; src/FileManager.Service/Program.cs:158

#### `FileManager.Contracts.IPC.IpcResponse and all 16 derived records (OkResponse … RelocateProfilesResponse)`

Same polymorphic "type" discriminator contract on the response side. IpcSerializer deliberately serializes through the BASE JsonTypeInfo — serializing as the derived type drops the discriminator and silently breaks the wire. Frame ORDER in the dry-run stream (chunks → progress → complete) is also contractual.

*Mechanism:* serialization

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IpcResponse.cs:10; src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IpcSerializer.cs:16

#### `FileManager.Contracts.IPC.EngineEvent and derived (JobStartedEvent, JobProgressEvent, JobCompletedEvent, JobFailedEvent, PauseChangedEvent, ProfilesChangedEvent, RunQueuedEvent, EngineWarningEvent)`

Broadcast wire format with "type" discriminators. JobPhase's MEMBER ORDER is behaviorally load-bearing: the progress publisher drops any sample whose phase went backwards, so reordering members changes runtime behavior.

*Mechanism:* serialization

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/EngineEvent.cs:7; src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/EngineEvent.cs:24

#### `IpcRequest.CurrentProtocolVersion / IpcRequest.ProtocolVersion`

Version 6 handshake. A mismatched service/UI pair must fail loud with IPC_VERSION_MISMATCH. Any change to the request/response/event shapes requires a documented version bump, not a silent edit — the UI and service ship as separate executables and can be at different versions on one machine.

*Mechanism:* serialization

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IpcRequest.cs:39; src/FileManager.Core/IPC/IpcServer.cs:241

#### `FileManager.Core.Journal.JournalRecord and all 12 derived records (JobOpenedRecord … JobClosedRecord)`

Write-ahead journal on disk (journal-NNNNNN.ndjsonl) read back by crash recovery at every service start. Discriminators are the short strings "open"/"sealed"/"twb"/"tver"/"tstg"/"tplc"/"tunc"/"tskp"/"commit"/"rbbegin"/"trb"/"close" under property name "t". A journal written before a crash MUST still replay — renaming a record, a property, or a discriminator loses in-flight user data.

*Mechanism:* serialization

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/Journal/JournalRecord.cs:8; src/FileManager.Core/Journal/JournalRecord.cs:114

#### `FileManager.Core.Journal.RollbackAction, FileManager.Core.Jobs.JobOutcome, FileManager.Core.Jobs.SkipReason (and the PolicySnapshot enums)`

JournalJsonContext has no UseStringEnumConverter, so these serialize as INTEGERS into the on-disk journal. Member DECLARATION ORDER is the wire contract — new members must be appended only; reordering or removing one makes an existing journal replay as a different action. Explicitly annotated as such in-source.

*Mechanism:* serialization

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/Journal/JournalRecord.cs:94; src/FileManager.Core/Journal/JournalRecord.cs:109; src/FileManager.Core/Jobs/Job.cs:241

#### `FileManager.Core.Jobs.JobOutcome member NAMES ("Succeeded", "Skipped", "Failed", "RollbackFailed") and SkipReason names`

Stringified with .ToString() into JobSummaryDto.Outcome/SkipReason on the wire, and the UI switches on the STRING LITERALS to pick status text, icon key and brush key. Renaming an enum member compiles cleanly on both sides and silently degrades every activity row to the "Unknown" icon.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/IPC/Handlers/GetRecentJobsHandler.cs:29; src/FileManager.UI/ViewModels/ActivityViewModel.cs:98

Persisted as settings.json (SchemaVersion 4) and re-read by BOTH the service and, independently, the UI at startup. Back-compat migration shim: pre-v2 settings.json is re-read as a raw JsonDocument to carry a pinned worker count into ScanThreading.MaxHashThreads. These string literals are the only remaining trace of the old schema — deleting MigrateLegacy as 'dead code' silently drops a user's pinned setting.

#### `FileManager.Core.DryRun.FileEvaluation / PhysicalFile / VirtualFileOperation and Contracts.DryRun.OperationKind`

The dry-run spool spill file (*.snapshot) is HAND-WRITTEN and HAND-READ with UTF-8 literal property names ("SourceFile", "SourceOp", "DestinationFiles", "DestinationOps", "Path", "Root", "Length", "LastWritten", "IsReparsePoint", "Kind", "SourceIndex", "SubjectIndex", "SourceDisposition", "Detail"). The writer and reader are two halves of one format that must change together, and OperationKind/OnSuccessAction are written as INTEGERS, so their member order is load-bearing for any snapshot left on disk.

*Mechanism:* serialization

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/DryRun/DryRunSnapshotFormat.cs:61; src/FileManager.Core/DryRun/DryRunSnapshotFormat.cs:103; src/FileManager.Core/DryRun/DryRunSnapshotFormat.cs:201

#### `FileManager.Contracts.DryRun.DryRunReport, DryRunDirectory, DryRunFile, DryRunOperation, SpaceProjection, DryRunProgress`

Streamed over IPC as chunk frames. LIST ORDER is a hard contract — SourceIndex/SubjectIndex/DirIndex/ParentIndex/RootDirIndex are integer positions into the assembled lists, so the engine's emit order must equal the client's assembly order. Any 'cleanup' that reorders, filters, or re-sorts a collection corrupts every cross-reference.

*Mechanism:* serialization

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Contracts/DryRun/DryRunReport.cs:18; src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IpcResponse.cs:73

Selector strings match on class names applied in markup/code, and PART_ names reach INTO the Fluent theme's and TreeDataGrid's control templates. Both are pure string coupling to third-party internals — renaming a class or upgrading the vendored control can silently drop styling.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.UI/Themes/Controls.axaml:38; src/FileManager.UI/Themes/Controls.axaml:300

#### `All 17 IIpcRequestHandler implementations (GetStatusHandler … ShutdownHandler) and their RequestType strings`

Registered one-by-one in the composition root and folded into a Dictionary<string, IIpcRequestHandler> keyed by handler.RequestType. There is NO assembly scanning (AOT constraint), so a handler that is renamed/moved but not re-registered compiles and simply stops answering; a handler added to the DI list but missing from IpcRequestTypes answers NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Note DryRunStreamHandler is an IIpcStreamingRequestHandler and throws from HandleAsync by design.

*Mechanism:* di-registration

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Service/Program.cs:136; src/FileManager.Core/IPC/IIpcServer.cs:20; src/FileManager.Core/IPC/Handlers/DryRunStreamHandler.cs:57

#### `Every Core interface/implementation pair registered in Program.cs (IFileSystemService, IFilterCompiler, IProfileValidator, IProfileStore, IProfileCatalog, ISettingsProvider, IScanScheduler, ISourceScanner, IFileHasher, IConflictResolver, IDryRunEngine, IJobJournal, IDispositionAuditLog, ITransientRetryPolicy, IDiskPreflight, IAtomicPlacer, IRollbackExecutor, ISourceDispositionService, ICrashRecovery, IPauseStateService, IEngineEventBus, IJobLogStore, ITriggerQueue, IProfileMatcher, IJobExecutor, IJobOrchestrator) plus the Windows adapters (WindowsIpcEndpointProvider, WindowsAutostartRegistrar, WindowsVolumeInfoProvider, WindowsMetadataPreserver, WindowsTrashService, WindowsPathCanonicalizer)`

Explicit singleton registration by type — no convention-based discovery. Splitting a class into two, or introducing a second implementation, requires editing the composition root; the DI graph fails at RUNTIME (host build), not compile time, and EngineHost's constructor injection list must be kept in step.

*Mechanism:* di-registration

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Service/Program.cs:67; src/FileManager.Service/Program.cs:97; src/FileManager.Service/EngineHost.cs:22

#### `IPC error CODE string literals: IPC_VERSION_MISMATCH, IPC_TRANSPORT, IPC_MALFORMED, IPC_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE, IPC_INTERNAL, JOB_LOG_NOT_FOUND, PROFILE_NOT_FOUND, PROFILE_INACTIVE, PATH_OUT_OF_SCOPE, PATH_NOT_FOUND, DRY_RUN_FAILED, CANCELED, PROFILES_RELOCATE_FAILED, SETTINGS_SAVE_FAILED, NOT_IMPLEMENTED, INTERNAL_ERROR`

Produced as free strings in Core handlers and MATCHED as string literals in the UI to drive behavior (reconnect on IPC_TRANSPORT, 'no log yet' on JOB_LOG_NOT_FOUND, transport-specific error text on dry run). There is no shared constant — the two sides are coupled only by the literal.

*Mechanism:* string-reference

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.UI/Services/IpcGateway.cs:248; src/FileManager.UI/ViewModels/ActivityViewModel.cs:312; src/FileManager.Core/IPC/Handlers/GetJobLogHandler.cs:26

#### `ProfileValidator issue CODE strings (PROFILE_SCHEMA_VERSION, PROFILE_NO_SOURCES, PROFILE_NO_TARGETS, PROFILE_TARGET_EQUALS_SOURCE, PROFILE_PATH_INVALID, PROFILE_UNVERIFIED_DELETE, PROFILE_HIGH_RISK_SOURCE, PROFILE_CYCLE_WARN, …)`

Cross the wire inside ValidationIssue, are displayed to the user, are enumerated into log/warning text by the UI, and are the normative code table in the architecture spec. They are documentation-level API even though nothing outside the repo consumes them.

*Mechanism:* string-reference

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/Profiles/ProfileValidator.cs:237; src/FileManager.UI/ViewModels/MainWindowViewModel.cs:567; docs/specs/architecture-v1.md:327

#### `FileManager.Platform.Windows.WindowsTrashService COM interfaces (IFileOperation {947aab5f-0a5c-4c13-b4d6-4bf7836fc9f8}, IShellItem {43826d1e-e718-42ee-bc55-a1e261c37bfe}) and all [LibraryImport] declarations in WindowsVolumeInfoProvider / WindowsPathCanonicalizer`

[GeneratedComInterface] method DECLARATION ORDER is the COM vtable layout — reordering or inserting a method silently calls the wrong shell function and can delete the wrong file. LibraryImport entry points (GetDiskFreeSpaceExW, GetDriveTypeW, GetDiskFreeSpaceW, GetLongPathNameW) and their marshalling attributes are an OS ABI contract.

*Mechanism:* interop

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Platform.Windows/WindowsTrashService.cs:125; src/FileManager.Platform.Windows/WindowsTrashService.cs:132; src/FileManager.Platform.Windows/WindowsVolumeInfoProvider.cs:173

#### `ServiceLauncher ("FileManager.Service.exe", FILEMANAGER_SERVICE_EXE) and IpcEndpoint ("filemanager-<user>", FILEMANAGER_PIPE_NAME) + the single-instance mutex name Local\FileManager.Service.<user>`

Cross-PROCESS contract, not compiler-visible: the UI probes for the service exe by literal FILE NAME beside itself, and both processes derive the same pipe name from duplicated (deliberately, per §4.11) logic in Contracts and Core.Platform. Renaming the service assembly, changing the pipe derivation on one side only, or 'deduplicating' IpcEndpoint into Core breaks launch/connect at runtime. The env-var names are a documented external override surface.

*Mechanism:* string-reference

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/ServiceLauncher.cs:16; src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IpcEndpoint.cs:9; src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IpcEndpoint.cs:20; src/FileManager.Service/EngineHost.cs:66

#### `WindowsAutostartRegistrar registry coordinates: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, value name "FileManager.Service"`

Writes into the user's live registry. Changing the value name orphans an existing autostart entry on every machine that already registered — the old entry keeps launching a stale path and unregister becomes a no-op.

*Mechanism:* string-reference

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Platform.Windows/WindowsAutostartRegistrar.cs:16

#### `FileManager.Core.Files.InfrastructurePaths constants: ".fm_staging", ".pipeline_tmp", ".fmtmp-" and StagedPathFor's layout <root>/.fm_staging/<jobId:N>/<index>-<name>`

These names exist ON USER DISKS: every scan/sweep skips them, crash recovery locates orphaned staged content by this exact path shape, and the placer's temp-file suffix is parsed back (marker + hex). Changing a name or the staged-path layout makes existing staged priors unrecoverable AND makes leftover infrastructure files visible as user content to the next scan.

*Mechanism:* string-reference

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/Files/InfrastructurePaths.cs:13; src/FileManager.Core/Files/InfrastructurePaths.cs:22; src/FileManager.Core/Files/InfrastructurePaths.cs:88

#### `FileManager.Core.EnginePaths and its mirror FileManager.UI.Services.UiPaths`

UiPaths deliberately DUPLICATES EnginePaths.Default() because the UI may reference Contracts only (§1 rule 3). GlobalSettings.DefaultProfilesDirectory is a THIRD copy that must equal EnginePaths.ProfilesDirectory or an existing install loses its profiles. This is sanctioned duplication — consolidating it violates the layering rule; changing one copy without the others is a data-loss bug.

*Mechanism:* string-reference

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/EnginePaths.cs:41; src/FileManager.UI/Services/UiPaths.cs:8; src/FileManager.Contracts/Settings/GlobalSettings.cs:107

#### `FileManager.Core.Journal.NdjsonFrame ("J1 <crc:x8> <json>\n")`

Line framing shared by the journal and the audit log, both append-only files that already exist on disk. The "J1" prefix is a format version; changing framing or the checksum function invalidates every stored line (decode returns 'unknown frame version'/'crc mismatch'). Note it is INTERNAL to Core but consumed by two subsystems — do not scope it down further.

*Mechanism:* serialization

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/Journal/NdjsonFrame.cs:15; src/FileManager.Core/Audit/DispositionAuditLog.cs:27

#### `FileManager.Contracts.IPC.IpcFrameCodec (4-byte little-endian length prefix, MaxPayloadBytes = 16 MiB, ConnectionClosedMessage = "connection closed")`

Transport framing used symmetrically by the Contracts-side client and the Core-side server. The 16 MiB cap is why streamed dry runs exist at all; ConnectionClosedMessage is compared as a STRING to distinguish clean EOF from a fault.

*Mechanism:* serialization

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IpcFrameCodec.cs:16; src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IpcFrameCodec.cs:20

#### `All JsonSerializerContext partials: FileManagerJsonContext, JournalJsonContext, AuditJsonContext, StateJsonContext, UiJsonContext, DryRunSnapshotJsonContext`

Source-generated, AOT-required serialization roots. Every serializable type must be listed with [JsonSerializable]; a type that is moved/renamed but not re-listed fails at RUNTIME under AOT (no reflection fallback). The split between them is intentional isolation — internal on-disk shapes must never be folded into the public FileManagerJsonContext.

*Mechanism:* serialization

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Contracts/FileManagerJsonContext.cs:10; src/FileManager.Core/Watching/StateJsonContext.cs:12; src/FileManager.Core/DryRun/DryRunSnapshotJsonContext.cs:10

### Persisted formats (12)

*On-disk layouts and their compatibility rules.*

#### `profiles/*.json — one file per profile, file name is the Guid in "D" format; written atomically (random temp + fsync + rename)`

*Risk if changed:* The whole Profile graph is frozen. The directory is USER-RELOCATABLE (settings.ProfilesDirectory, resolved live on every read), so any code that caches or hard-codes the profile directory breaks relocation. A load failure is a silent skip with a log warning — a schema break shows up as profiles quietly disappearing from the list, not as an error.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/Profiles/ProfileStore.cs:130; src/FileManager.Core/Profiles/ProfileStore.cs:196

#### `settings.json (single file at the engine root, SchemaVersion 4) — written by the service, read INDEPENDENTLY by the UI at startup for the theme`

*Risk if changed:* Two readers, one writer, across two processes and two assemblies. A corrupt/unloadable file falls back to defaults SILENTLY — a property rename does not error, it resets the user's settings. The v1→v2 migration shim (raw JsonDocument) must survive.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/Settings/SettingsService.cs:55; src/FileManager.UI/Services/StartupTheme.cs:29

#### `journal/journal-NNNNNN.ndjsonl — append-only, fsync'd write-ahead log, 'J1 <crc32:x8> <json>\n' per line, rotated by size`

*Risk if changed:* HIGHEST data-loss risk in the repo. Crash recovery MUST replay journals written by the previous build before the IPC server starts (I-RECOVER-FIRST). Enums serialize as INTEGERS here. Any change to a record type, discriminator, property, enum ordering, or the frame prefix makes in-flight jobs unrecoverable and can strand or destroy staged user files.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/Journal/JobJournal.cs:320; src/FileManager.Core/Journal/NdjsonFrame.cs:21

#### `audit/audit-YYYYMM.ndjsonl — deletion audit trail, monthly files, NEVER auto-deleted, same J1 framing`

*Risk if changed:* Unbounded retention means records of arbitrary age must still parse. The reader only reads the 1 MiB tail and skips malformed lines with a warning, so a format break degrades to silently empty audit history.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/Audit/DispositionAuditLog.cs:137

#### `state/pause.json — { "paused": bool }`

*Risk if changed:* A shape change resets the global pause flag; the engine would resume processing on a machine the user had paused.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/Watching/StateJsonContext.cs:5

#### `<scratch>/*.snapshot — dry-run spool spill files, hand-written/hand-read trimmed JSON`

*Risk if changed:* Same-machine, same-version by design (each run deletes its own; startup purges leftovers), so the format is comparatively free — BUT the writer and reader are two halves of one hand-maintained format with omitted-field reconstruction (source op path/root, subject-targeting dest op path). Change one half only and records deserialize with the WRONG PATHS rather than failing.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/DryRun/DryRunSnapshotFormat.cs:57; src/FileManager.Service/EngineHost.cs:177

#### `logs/jobs/<jobId:N>.log and rolling logs/service-YYYYMMDD.log, logs/ui-YYYYMMDD.log (14-day retention)`

*Risk if changed:* Job logs are fetched over IPC by job id; the file name derivation is the lookup key. The UI's log-folder action and the service's writer must agree on the directory.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/Observability/JobLogStore.cs:120; src/FileManager.Service/Program.cs:47; src/FileManager.UI/Program.cs:24

#### `%LOCALAPPDATA%\FileManager\ui-state.json — client-side sidebar layout`

*Risk if changed:* Read/write failures are swallowed and fall back to defaults; a schema break silently resets layout. Deliberately NOT part of GlobalSettings — do not merge it in.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.UI/Services/UiStateStore.cs:24

#### `Exported profile .json (single profile, on-disk format, written atomically, never overwriting)`

*Risk if changed:* An INTERCHANGE format: exported files must round-trip back through Import, including files exported by older builds and files shared between machines. Uses the same FileManagerJsonContext.Profile as the profile store, so it inherits the whole frozen graph.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.UI/Services/ProfileExport.cs:27

#### `IPC wire: 4-byte LE length prefix + UTF-8 JSON, 16 MiB frame cap, over named pipe filemanager-<user>; ProtocolVersion 6 handshake`

*Risk if changed:* UI and service are separate executables that can be at different versions on one machine, and the service may already be RUNNING (started at logon) when a new UI connects. Any message-shape change requires a protocol version bump; without one, the pair half-parses instead of failing loud.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IpcFrameCodec.cs:16; src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IpcRequest.cs:39; src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IpcEndpoint.cs:20

#### `On-disk infrastructure markers inside USER target roots: <root>/.fm_staging/<jobId:N>/<index>-<name>, <tempRoot>/.pipeline_tmp/<jobId>/, <finalName>.fmtmp-<hex>`

*Risk if changed:* These sit inside the user's own folders. Crash recovery finds staged PRIOR VERSIONS of overwritten user files by this exact path shape; scans exclude them by name. Change either and recovery cannot restore what it staged, or the tool's own temp files start being treated as user content to copy.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Core/Files/InfrastructurePaths.cs:22; src/FileManager.Core/Files/InfrastructurePaths.cs:88

#### `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run value "FileManager.Service" = "<quoted ProcessPath>"`

*Risk if changed:* Live OS state on the user's machine; both register and unregister key off the literal value name. Also assumes a self-contained deployment where ProcessPath IS the service exe.

*Evidence:* src/FileManager.Platform.Windows/WindowsAutostartRegistrar.cs:16

VENDORED third-party source, tracked as a git submodule (350 files) built from MIT source instead of the NuGet package to avoid the Avalonia Pro license gate. ### Constraint notes

- SCOPE NOTE: `git ls-files` outside src/tests/benchmarks was searched too. Nothing in the repo does assembly scanning, `Activator.CreateInstance`, `Type.GetType`, or attribute-driven discovery of application types — the architecture spec FORBIDS them (AOT constraint) and every dispatch is an explicit table. The only reflection in shipping code is `EnumTitleExtensions.GetTitle` reading `[Tooltip]` off enum FIELD NAMES (src/FileManager.UI/Extensions/EnumTitleExtensions.cs:16), and reflection in tests that pins contracts (tests/FileManager.Core.Tests/IPC/IpcRequestTypesTests.cs:17 enumerates `[JsonDerivedType]`). So the compiler-invisible coupling here is NOT reflection — it is (a) persisted formats, (b) XAML, (c) hand-maintained parallel tables.

THREE HAND-MAINTAINED PARALLEL TABLES. Each must be edited together; the compiler checks none of the cross-links:
1. IpcRequest `[JsonDerivedType]` ↔ IpcRequestTypes consts + DiscriminatorOf switch ↔ handler.RequestType ↔ Program.cs DI list. (Guarded, partially: IpcRequestTypesTests pins 1↔2. Nothing pins the DI list — a handler missing there just answers NOT_IMPLEMENTED.)
2. EnginePaths.Default() ↔ UiPaths ↔ GlobalSettings.DefaultProfilesDirectory/DefaultScratchDirectory. Sanctioned duplication (§1 rule 3: UI may reference Contracts only). Do NOT propose consolidating these into a shared type — that would break the layering rule. Do flag them if one drifts.
3. IpcEndpoint.Resolve() (Contracts, client side) ↔ WindowsIpcEndpointProvider (Core/Platform, server side). Deliberately duplicated per §4.11.

LAYERING IS A HARD CONSTRAINT ON MOVES. References point strictly downward: Contracts (BCL only) ← Core ← Platform.Windows ← hosts. Core must contain zero OS-specific code (the single sanctioned `OperatingSystem.IsWindows()` probe is NormalizedPath's case-sensitivity at src/FileManager.Core/Jobs/Job.cs:38). UI and any future CLI reference Contracts ONLY — never Core. So "move this shared helper to Core" is illegal for anything the UI uses, and "move this type to Contracts" is only legal if it needs nothing outside the BCL.

AOT/TRIM IS A CONSTRAINT ON TECHNIQUE. Core, Contracts and Platform.Windows are IsAotCompatible/IsTrimmable; both exes PublishAot. Any refactor that introduces reflection-based serialization, `Activator.CreateInstance`, runtime proxies, classic COM interop attributes, or config-binding frameworks compiles fine and fails only in a published build. Every serializable type must be listed in a JsonSerializerContext.

COMPILED BINDINGS COVER MOST XAML — BUT NOT ALL. `AvaloniaUseCompiledBindingsByDefault=true` means most binding-path typos are build errors. The exceptions are four `x:CompileBindings="False"` regions in DryRunView.axaml (lines 62, 111, 506, 644) plus every DataTemplate `DataType=` type key in SettingsWindow.axaml and every resource-key string emitted from view models — all resolved at RUNTIME. Treat DryRunTreeNode / DryRunFileRow / DryRunDestinationRow command names, the setting-editor view-model type names, and the Icon*/Brush.* key strings as a public API.

ORDER-AS-CONTRACT (three places where reordering members changes behavior, not just names): JobPhase declaration order (progress publisher drops backwards samples); VerificationMethod / RollbackAction / JobOutcome / SkipReason ordinals (journal writes enums as ints); DryRunReport's four list orders (ops reference files by integer index, and the streaming client appends chunks in receive order).

WHAT LOOKS LIKE DEAD CODE BUT IS NOT: `DryRunSnapshotJsonContext` (src/FileManager.Core/DryRun/DryRunSnapshotJsonContext.cs:10) is unused by production — it is retained ON PURPOSE as the naïve full-record baseline that the read-back benchmark measures the trimmed hand-written format against. `SettingsService.MigrateLegacy` is a back-compat shim for pre-v2 settings.json. Profile members marked `[reserved — fails v1 validation]` (SyncMode.Mirror, VerificationMethod.SizeTimestamp, ArgumentMode.Shell, FilterSet.ContentHashDedupe) are deliberate extension points, not unimplemented cruft — Mirror in particular IS live in the dry-run path.

THE 17 IPC HANDLERS ARE NOT A DUPLICATION CANDIDATE. They are the intentional replacement for reflection-based handler discovery (§4.9, AOT). Their shape similarity is the point.

GUARD TESTS THAT WILL CATCH SOME BREAKS (worth running after any change to the frozen surface): tests/FileManager.Core.Tests/IPC/IpcRequestTypesTests.cs (dispatch table vs. wire discriminators), tests/FileManager.Contracts.Tests/IPC/SerializationTests.cs, tests/FileManager.UI.Tests/ResourceKeyContractTests.cs (every icon/brush key a view model can emit resolves in the real App.axaml), and the *SmokeTests in tests/FileManager.UI.Tests (headless XAML load per window).

NOT PUBLIC API: nothing here is consumed as a library outside the repo — there are no NuGet packages produced and no public SDK. The external surface is instead operational: the FileManager.Service.exe file name, the named pipe, the HKCU Run value, the two env-var overrides (FILEMANAGER_SERVICE_EXE, FILEMANAGER_PIPE_NAME), and the on-disk layout under %LOCALAPPDATA%\FileManager.

## Roadmap

### Tier 1 — Safe wins

Small, local, low blast radius. Each is independently shippable. 8 items.

#### 1.1 Stop the Settings dialog from overwriting real settings after a failed load

*Findings:* `settings-save-after-failed-load-overwrites-real-settings` (severity: high, effort: trivial)

**Why now.** Highest impact-to-effort item in the entire review and it is one bool in one file. SettingsViewModel.LoadAsync returns early at :433 and :465 leaving the constructor defaults from :88-92 in place; SaveAsync (:479) is gated only on IsBusy and rebuilds a complete GlobalSettings at :525-541. The service is a separate process that can be mid-restart for ordinary reasons, so this is reachable by a user simply opening Settings at the wrong moment and changing the theme. Because ProfileStore resolves ProfilesDirectory live from settings on every read, the result is the user's entire profile list disappearing. Do this before anything else touches SettingsViewModel.

**Change (settings-save-after-failed-load-overwrites-real-settings).** In src/FileManager.UI/ViewModels/SettingsViewModel.cs add `private bool _loadFailed;`. Set `_loadFailed = true` on both early-return error paths of LoadAsync (the IPC error branch at line 433 and the catch at line 465) and `_loadFailed = false` immediately after the successful mapping block completes (after line 463). At the top of SaveAsync's try, before building any dictionaries, add:
```
if (_loadFailed)
{
    ErrorMessage = "Settings could not be loaded, so saving would overwrite your stored settings with defaults. Close and reopen this window once the service is reachable.";
    return;
}
```
Do not gate SaveCommand.CanExecute on it — the existing tests in tests/FileManager.UI.Tests/SettingsViewModelTests.cs construct the VM and call SaveCommand without ever calling LoadAsync, and must keep passing (_loadFailed stays false there).

*Blast radius:* 1 file, 2 call sites.

One production file. LoadAsync has 2 failure exits and SaveAsync 1 entry point. 18 existing SaveCommand test invocations across SettingsViewModelTests.cs and SettingsViewModelUndoTests.cs never call LoadAsync, so none change behaviour.

*Prerequisites:* none.

*Verify:* Add a fact to tests/FileManager.UI.Tests/SettingsViewModelTests.cs: FakeIpcGateway returns an IpcError from GetSettingsAsync, await vm.LoadAsync(), await vm.SaveCommand.ExecuteAsync(null), assert gateway.SaveSettingsCalls is empty and ErrorMessage is non-null. Do NOT gate SaveCommand.CanExecute on the new flag — the 18 existing SaveCommand tests construct the VM without ever calling LoadAsync and must stay green.

#### 1.2 Quarantine an unparseable settings.json instead of letting the next save destroy it

*Findings:* `corrupt-settings-file-silently-replaced-by-defaults` (severity: low, effort: trivial)

**Why now.** Same failure family as the item above and the same file on disk; doing them together means one round of reasoning about settings persistence. SettingsService.Load returns GlobalSettings.Default from its catches at :97-107 and from the deserialized-to-null branch at :90, leaving the unreadable file in place for the next atomic Update to overwrite. Six defensive lines make a hand-corrupted or disk-corrupted file recoverable rather than permanently lost. Keep the fallback-to-defaults behavior — refusing to start on a bad settings file is worse.

**Change (corrupt-settings-file-silently-replaced-by-defaults).** In src/FileManager.Core/Settings/SettingsService.Load, before returning GlobalSettings.Default from either catch (lines 97-107) and from the deserialized-to-null branch at line 90, preserve the original: wrap in its own try/catch and `File.Move(file, file + ".corrupt-" + DateTime.UtcNow.ToString("yyyyMMddHHmmss"), overwrite: false)`, logging at Error (not Warning) with both paths. This makes the subsequent Update a fresh write rather than a destructive overwrite and leaves the user's configuration recoverable by hand. Keep the fallback-to-defaults behaviour itself — refusing to start the service on a bad settings file is worse.

*Blast radius:* 1 file, 3 call sites.

SettingsService.cs only; three return-defaults sites inside the private Load method, which is called exactly once from the constructor (line 39).

*Prerequisites:* Settings-save guard landed (same subsystem, avoids merge conflict)

```csharp
services.AddSingleton<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, IIpcRequestHandler>>(provider =>
{
    Dictionary<string, IIpcRequestHandler> table = new(StringComparer.Ordinal);
    foreach (IIpcRequestHandler handler in provider.GetServices<IIpcRequestHandler>())

    return table;
});
```

This is DI enumeration of explicit registrations, not assembly scanning or reflection — it stays within the §1 AOT constraint (`GetServices<T>` over concrete registered types is AOT-safe and needs `using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;`, already imported). #### 2.1 Consolidate the staged-overwrite replace primitive and fix the non-idempotent recovery copy

*Findings:* `staged-replace-fallback-duplicated` (severity: medium, effort: small)

**Why now.** The single most valuable behavior-preserving change in the review, and it fixes a real latent bug rather than tidying. AtomicPlacer.TwoStepReplace guards its fallback with `if (File.Exists(finalPath))` and its doc states the idempotency is mandatory because 'a retry after the first move succeeded but the second failed would throw FileNotFound forever and strand the final name absent'. CrashRecovery.Replace at :470-478 does the same two moves unguarded — and it is called from the replay path that re-runs the same journal rows on EVERY service start, which is precisely the re-run scenario the guard was written for. Extract src/FileManager.Core/Files/StagedReplace.cs with the idempotent body and call it from both sites. Do NOT fold in RollbackExecutor.TryReplace — it replaces in the opposite direction with a null backup and overwrite:true, a genuinely different operation. Keep CrashRecovery's recovery-specific LogError+rethrow catch-all in place around the call.

**Change (staged-replace-fallback-duplicated).** Add src/FileManager.Core/Files/StagedReplace.cs:

```csharp
namespace FileManager.Core.Files;

/// <summary>The staged-overwrite primitive (§4.3, I-PRIOR): swap <paramref name="tempPath"/> into
/// <paramref name="finalPath"/> while the prior version lands at <paramref name="stagedPath"/>.
/// One Win32 ReplaceFile when the volume supports it; otherwise an IDEMPOTENT two-step move so a
/// retry (live placer) or a re-run (crash recovery) after a partial attempt still completes.</summary>
internal static class StagedReplace
{
    public static void Execute(string tempPath, string finalPath, string stagedPath, ILogger logger)
    {
        try { File.Replace(tempPath, finalPath, stagedPath, ignoreMetadataErrors: true); }
        catch (Exception ex) when (ex is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException or PlatformNotSupportedException)
        {
            logger.LogWarning(ex, "File.Replace rejected for {Final}; falling back to two-step move", finalPath);
            if (File.Exists(finalPath))
            {
                Directory.CreateDirectory(Path.GetDirectoryName(stagedPath)!);
                File.Move(finalPath, stagedPath, overwrite: false);
            }
            File.Move(tempPath, finalPath, overwrite: false);
        }
    }
}
```

Delete AtomicPlacer.ReplaceWithStaging and AtomicPlacer.TwoStepReplace; at AtomicPlacer.cs:310 call `StagedReplace.Execute(tempPath, finalPath, stagedPath, logger);`. In CrashRecovery replace the body of `Replace` (:470) with a call to `StagedReplace.Execute(temp, final, staged, logger);` inside the existing outer try that keeps its `LogError`+rethrow catch-all (:479-485) — that catch-all is recovery-specific and must stay. Do NOT fold in RollbackExecutor.TryReplace (Journal/RollbackExecutor.cs:287): it replaces in the opposite direction (staged → final) with `destinationBackupFileName: null` and an overwrite:true fallback, a genuinely different operation.

*Blast radius:* 3 files, 2 call sites.

Call sites: src/FileManager.Core/Placement/AtomicPlacer.cs:310 and src/FileManager.Core/Journal/CrashRecovery.cs:274. New file src/FileManager.Core/Files/StagedReplace.cs. RollbackExecutor.cs:287 deliberately excluded.

*Prerequisites:* None — but write the new CrashRecovery characterization test FIRST and confirm it fails on today's code

It fails before the change and passes after; that is the proof. tests/FileManager.Core.Tests/Placement/AtomicPlacerTests.cs must stay green unchanged (the placer's behavior does not move).

#### 2.4 Give the three catalog-mutating handlers one answer to a failed reload

*Findings:* `catalog-reload-failure-three-semantics` (severity: medium, effort: small)

**Why now.** SaveProfileHandler.cs:31-33 and DeleteProfileHandler.cs:25-27 log a warning and report success; RelocateProfilesHandler.cs:122-129 returns an ErrorResponse with a comment stating exactly why ('the catalog would keep serving the old directory's snapshot'). ProfileCatalog.Reload returns early on failure without swapping the snapshot or notifying subscribers, so on that path the service serves a stale catalog, broadcasts no ProfilesChangedEvent, and tells the client OK — while RunProfileHandler.cs:41 resolves the job's profile from that stale catalog.All, including a stale OnSuccessAction that may be PermanentDelete. Extract one CatalogReloadGuard and use it in all three. Reuse the existing PROFILE_SAVE_FAILED / PROFILE_DELETE_FAILED codes; keep relocate's existing message wording rather than forcing it into a shared template. The message must say plainly that the mutation DID reach disk but the list could not be refreshed.

**Change (catalog-reload-failure-three-semantics).** Give the three handlers one rule. Add src/FileManager.Core/IPC/Handlers/CatalogReloadGuard.cs:

    internal static class CatalogReloadGuard
    {
        /// Returns null when the reload succeeded, else the ErrorResponse the handler must return.
        public static ErrorResponse? Check(IProfileCatalog catalog, ILogger logger, string code, string didWhat)
        {
            Result reload = catalog.Reload();
            if (!reload.TryGetError(out string? error)) return null;
            logger.LogError("Catalog reload after {DidWhat} failed: {Error}", didWhat, error);
            return new ErrorResponse { Code = code, Message = $"the profile was {didWhat}, but reloading the profile list failed: {error}; retry, or restart the service" };
        }
    }

In SaveProfileHandler.HandleAsync replace lines 31-33 with `if (CatalogReloadGuard.Check(catalog, logger, "PROFILE_SAVE_FAILED", "saved") is { } failure) return Task.FromResult<IpcResponse>(failure);`. In DeleteProfileHandler replace lines 25-27 with the same call using "PROFILE_DELETE_FAILED" / "deleted". In RelocateProfilesHandler replace lines 122-129 with the call using "PROFILES_RELOCATE_FAILED" / $"relocated to \"{newDir}\"" so all three share one definition.

The UI already handles an ErrorResponse on both routes (IpcGateway.SaveProfileAsync at src/FileManager.UI/Services/IpcGateway.cs:48 and DeleteProfileAsync at line 58 both surface IpcError), so no client change is needed. Reuse the existing PROFILE_SAVE_FAILED / PROFILE_DELETE_FAILED codes rather than inventing new ones — the UI matches neither by string, it only displays the message.

*Blast radius:* 4 files, 3 call sites.

Three catalog.Reload() call sites in src/FileManager.Core/IPC/Handlers/ (SaveProfileHandler.cs:31, DeleteProfileHandler.cs:25, RelocateProfilesHandler.cs:122) plus one new file. The fourth Reload() in the repo, EngineHost.cs:91, is the startup load and is deliberately non-fatal — leave it.

*Prerequisites:* none.

*Verify:* tests/FileManager.Core.Tests/IPC/RelocateProfilesHandlerTests.cs pins the relocate branch and must stay green. Save and Delete have no dedicated tests — add two direct handler tests with an IProfileCatalog double whose Reload() fails, asserting ErrorResponse rather than ValidationResponse/OkResponse. Run EndToEndSmokeTests to confirm the happy path is unchanged. No UI change needed: IpcGateway.SaveProfileAsync/DeleteProfileAsync already surface IpcError.

#### 2.6 Make EngineHost constructible by a test and pin the startup ordering

*Findings:* `enginehost-startup-sequence-unreachable` (severity: medium, effort: small)

**Why now.** I-RECOVER-FIRST is the invariant that keeps a crashed job's staged prior versions of user files recoverable: if the IPC server or the orchestrator starts before CrashRecovery.Recover returns, a new job can take path locks over files recovery was about to restore. CrashRecovery itself has 1085 lines of tests; that it is CALLED FIRST is asserted nowhere, and the three lifetime.StopApplication() early exits at :111, :120 and :147 have never been executed by a test. Two production edits — InternalsVisibleTo in FileManager.Service.csproj, and an optional trailing `instanceMutexName` parameter so a test never contends with a real service on the developer's machine (keep the literal derivation inside EngineHost; it is a frozen cross-process contract). This is also the prerequisite for the Tier 3 composition-root extraction: without it, that extraction cannot be verified.

**Change (enginehost-startup-sequence-unreachable).** Two edits, then one new test file.

1. Add to src/FileManager.Service/FileManager.Service.csproj, inside a new ItemGroup:
   <InternalsVisibleTo Include="FileManager.Service.Tests" />
   (matching the existing declarations in src/FileManager.Core/FileManager.Core.csproj:26 and src/FileManager.UI/FileManager.UI.csproj:18).

2. In src/FileManager.Service/EngineHost.cs, add a trailing optional constructor parameter `string? instanceMutexName = null` and change line 64-66 to use `name: instanceMutexName ?? (@"Local\FileManager.Service." + IpcEndpoint.SanitizeUserName(Environment.UserName))`. Do NOT move the derivation out of EngineHost — the literal is a frozen cross-process contract. This exists only so a test never contends with a real service running on the developer's machine.

3. Add tests/FileManager.Service.Tests/EngineHostStartupTests.cs. Construct EngineHost with NullLogger, a stub IHostApplicationLifetime that records StopApplication(), an EnginePaths pointed at a temp root, a unique instanceMutexName, TimeProvider.System, and recording fakes for IProfileCatalog / IIpcServer / ICrashRecovery / IJobOrchestrator / IEngineEventBus / IPauseStateService / IAutostartRegistrar / ISettingsProvider. Each fake appends its own name to a shared List<string> ordering log. Call StartAsync/StopAsync and assert:
   - the ordering log is exactly ["catalog.Reload", "crashRecovery.Recover", "ipcServer.Start", "eventBus.Subscribe", "pauseState.Subscribe", "catalog.Subscribe", "orchestrator.Start"] — pinning I-RECOVER-FIRST and the bridges-after-Reload rule;
   - when ICrashRecovery returns a JobError, ipcServer.Start and orchestrator.Start are never called and StopApplication was invoked;
   - when IIpcServer.Start returns an error, orchestrator.Start is never called;

Assert the load-bearing ORDERING CONSTRAINTS — Reload before Recover, Recover before ipcServer.Start, bridges after Reload and before orchestrator.Start, orchestrator.StopAsync before ipcServer.StopAsync on shutdown — and the three early-exit paths (recovery failure and IPC-start failure each skip the rest and call StopApplication; a second host on the same mutex name exits without touching anything). #### 3.3 Introduce an IIpcConnection seam and test IpcGateway's reconnect rules

*Findings:* `ipcgateway-no-coverage-static-transport` (severity: medium, effort: medium)

**Why now.** IpcGateway is the UI's only path to the service — 328 lines owning the shared-client cache, the poison-recycle rule, the error-code-driven drop rule and the deliberate connection isolation for events and dry runs — and it has no test file, because connections come from the statics ServiceLauncher.ConnectOrStartAsync and IpcClient.ConnectAsync over a sealed private-constructor type that only a real named pipe can produce (and FileManager.UI.Tests cannot serve one, since the UI references Contracts only). The consequence is that recovery from a service restart is entirely unverified, and the codes the drop rule matches (IPC_TRANSPORT, IPC_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE, IPC_MALFORMED) are free string literals with no shared constant, so a service-side rename breaks reconnect silently. Extract an IIpcConnection interface over IpcClient's exact existing public signatures (BCL-only, so it is legal in Contracts and stays AOT/trim-clean) and inject two connect delegates with production defaults so App.axaml.cs:34 keeps working. Judge this item on its own merits AFTER the shared-predicate item lands: it is worth doing only if the transport-recovery behavior is actually going to be maintained.

**Change (ipcgateway-no-coverage-static-transport).** Introduce one seam: an interface over the connection.

1. New file src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IIpcConnection.cs:
   public interface IIpcConnection : IAsyncDisposable {
       bool IsPoisoned { get; }
       Task<Result<TResponse, IpcError>> RequestAsync<TResponse>(IpcRequest request, CancellationToken ct = default) where TResponse : IpcResponse;
       Task<Result<DryRunReport, IpcError>> DryRunStreamAsync(DryRunStreamRequest request, IProgress<DryRunProgress>? progress = null, CancellationToken ct = default);
       IAsyncEnumerable<EngineEvent> SubscribeAsync(CancellationToken ct = default);
   }
   These are the exact existing public signatures of IpcClient — add `, IIpcConnection` to the declaration at src/FileManager.Contracts/IPC/IpcClient.cs:15 and change nothing else in that file. BCL-only, so it is legal in Contracts and stays AOT/trim-clean.

2. In src/FileManager.UI/Services/IpcGateway.cs: change the field at line 28 to `IIpcConnection? _client`, and add a constructor taking two delegates with production defaults:
   public IpcGateway(
       Func<CancellationToken, Task<Result<IIpcConnection, string>>>? connectOrStart = null,
       Func<CancellationToken, Task<Result<IIpcConnection, string>>>? connectOnly = null)
   defaulting to thin lambdas over ServiceLauncher.ConnectOrStartAsync (used at lines 173 and 287) and IpcClient.ConnectAsync (used at line 109). Keep the parameterless call site in App.axaml.cs:34 working via the defaults.

3. Add tests/FileManager.UI.Tests/IpcGatewayTests.cs with a FakeConnection : IIpcConnection that scripts per-request outcomes, an IsPoisoned flag, and a Disposed counter. Cover: the shared client is reused across two successive requests (connect delegate invoked once); an IPC_TRANSPORT / IPC_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE / IPC_MALFORMED error disposes the client and the next request connects a fresh one; a non-transport error code (e.g. PROFILE_NOT_FOUND) does NOT drop the client; IsPoisoned after a successful-looking response still drops; DryRunAsync and SubscribeEventsAsync each take their own connection and never touch the shared one; DisposeAsync followed by a request returns an IpcError rather than throwing ObjectDisposedException.

4. In the same file, add SaveProfileAsync tests over a FakeConnection returning a scripted ValidationResponse, asserting SaveOutcome.Saved for the four combinations (Error present; BlockingWarning with acknowledgeWarnings false; BlockingWarning with acknowledgeWarnings true; Info only) — mirroring the assertions in ProfileStoreTests so drift between the two copies of the rule becomes a red test.

*Blast radius:* 3 files, 1 call site.

`new IpcGateway()` appears exactly once (App.axaml.cs:34) and keeps working via defaulted parameters. Adding `IIpcConnection` to IpcClient is purely additive: the 4 files in tests/FileManager.Service.Tests that use the concrete IpcClient (EndToEndSmokeTests, IpcRobustnessTests, IpcServerOversizedResponseTests, IpcServerStreamingTests) are unaffected. 16 files in src/FileManager.UI depend on IIpcGateway, not IpcGateway, and are untouched.

*Prerequisites:* Tier 2: the save-blocking predicate already hoisted to Contracts — that removes the drift half of this finding, so what remains is purely the transport seam

*Verify:* All existing tests/FileManager.UI.Tests stay green unchanged (they only use IIpcGateway). New tests/FileManager.UI.Tests/IpcGatewayTests.cs with a FakeConnection scripting per-request outcomes, an IsPoisoned flag and a Disposed counter, covering: the shared client is reused across two requests (connect delegate invoked once); IPC_TRANSPORT / IPC_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE / IPC_MALFORMED each dispose the client and the next request reconnects; a non-transport code (PROFILE_NOT_FOUND) does NOT drop the client; IsPoisoned after a successful-looking response still drops; DryRunAsync and SubscribeEventsAsync each take their own connection; a request after DisposeAsync returns an IpcError rather than throwing. Then verify by hand: kill FileManager.Service.exe with the UI open, confirm the status bar goes disconnected, restart the service, confirm the UI reconnects on the next 2s poll without an app restart.

#### 3.4 Extract StorageBar's band layout so the space-warning thresholds can be cross-checked

*Findings:* `storagebar-band-layout-inside-render` (severity: low, effort: small)

**Why now.** Lowest-priority structural item; include only if the space-projection UI is being worked on. All of StorageBar's decision logic — band extents, the net-frees inversion when settled < used, the over-margin red/amber escalation, and the emission order that drives hover hit-testing — lives inside Render(DrawingContext) interleaved with DrawRectangle calls, reachable only through a real render pass. The threshold rule is deliberately written twice: VolumeSpaceRow's warning text (DryRunViewModel.cs:2169, tested) and StorageBar's colouring (StorageBar.cs:166, untested), linked only by a comment reading 'Warnings mirror the bar'. The repo already established the fix pattern in the same folder — PathText's rules were split into the UI-free PathTruncation precisely so they could be unit-tested. No drift has actually occurred, so the benefit is entirely prospective, and the extraction moves ordering-sensitive logic. The only part carrying real value is the cross-check test; the geometry extraction is its vehicle, not the goal.

**Change (storagebar-band-layout-inside-render).** Follow the PathTruncation precedent in src/FileManager.UI/Controls/.

1. New file src/FileManager.UI/Controls/StorageBandLayout.cs, no Avalonia types:

   internal static class StorageBandLayout {

Compute returns bands in the same emission order (the hit-test scans newest-first, so order is behavior).

2. Render becomes: `foreach (StorageBand b in StorageBandLayout.Compute(...))` → map Role+OverRed/OverAmber to the brush (the existing Band(...) palette lookup and the LabelLight/LabelDark choice stay in the control), clamp/scale to pixels, DrawRectangle, append to _bands, DrawLabel. MarginLineBytes replaces the inline `if (marginLine > 0 && marginLine < cap)` guard at line 190.

3. Add tests/FileManager.UI.Tests/StorageBandLayoutTests.cs covering: growth case (settled > used) emits CSU then SUAR then RPSU then APSU in that order; net-frees case (settled < used) emits SUAR then a Freed band and no CSU; zero-width bands (settled == used) are omitted; OverRed is set exactly when realisticPeak > capacity - margin and OverAmber exactly when safeCeiling > capacity - margin (add the boundary case where they are equal); a band whose To exceeds capacity is clamped; MarginLineBytes returns null when margin >= capacity or margin == 0. Add one cross-check test asserting Compute's OverRed/OverAmber agree with VolumeSpaceRow.IsDanger/IsWarning for the same inputs, so the two copies of the rule can no longer drift silently.

*Blast radius:* 2 files, 1 call site.

StorageBar is instantiated in exactly one place, src/FileManager.UI/Views/DryRunView.axaml:164. Its six styled properties are unchanged, so the XAML and the DryRunSpaceViewModel bindings are untouched. StorageBar is a type-independent control (no ControlTheme keyed by {x:Type}), so no theme coupling is at risk.

*Prerequisites:* None, but do not schedule ahead of anything above it

*Verify:* New StorageBandLayoutTests covering band order in the growth case, the net-frees case, omission of zero-width bands, OverRed/OverAmber exactly at and either side of the capacity-minus-margin boundary, clamping past capacity, and MarginLineBytes returning null outside (0, capacity). The load-bearing one is a cross-check asserting Compute's OverRed/OverAmber agree with VolumeSpaceRow.IsDanger/IsWarning for the same inputs. DryRunViewSmokeTests.Storage_panel_and_bars_lay_out_with_a_projection must still render headlessly. #### 3.5 DECISION REQUIRED (do not execute unilaterally): retire or keep the batched dry-run pipeline

*Findings:* `batched-dry-run-pipeline-has-no-production-client` (severity: low, effort: large)

**Why now.** Listed last and flagged as a product decision, not a refactor. IDryRunEngine exposes two complete simulation implementations of the same semantics; only SimulateStreamAsync has a client (the UI sends DryRunStreamRequest, and git shows the switch to streaming predates the current protocol version, so no protocol-6 client ever sends DryRunRequest). Retiring the batched half would remove ~250 lines of Core, a live IPC handler, and the maintenance of dry-run semantics in two pipelines — but it also deletes a handler, rewrites 12 tests on the safety-critical deletion-preview engine, drops the MaxReportBytes frame-cap machinery, and per its own migration story bumps IpcRequest.CurrentProtocolVersion 6→7 on a frozen cross-process surface where the service may already be running from an older build. Against that, DryRunEngine.cs:34 designates SimulateAsync as the batched/CLI path and docs/specs/architecture-v1.md:184 lists a planned FileManager.Cli.exe. So the question a human must answer is simply: is the batched/CLI dry run abandoned? If yes, execute the two-step plan (port coverage to SimulateStreamAsync first, verify green, then delete) and record the removal and the protocol bump in the spec. If no, leave it and keep the Tier 1 sweep-budget parity fix. NOTE THE CONFLICT: retiring this path makes the Tier 1 sweep-budget item moot, so if the decision is 'retire', do not spend effort maintaining parity in the meantime beyond the three-line fix already landed.

**Change (batched-dry-run-pipeline-has-no-production-client).** Two-step, in this order. (1) Port coverage: for each of the 12 SimulateAsync call sites in tests/FileManager.Core.Tests/DryRun/DryRunEngineTests.cs (:137, :273, :315, :456, :487, :606, :667) and DryRunPipelineTests.cs (:55, :107, :129, :168, :194, :284), rewrite the assertion against SimulateStreamAsync using the existing CollectStream helper in DryRunEngineTests; drop the two that assert only batched-specific byte-budget truncation (DryRunEngineTests.cs:273, :315) since MaxReportBytes disappears with the path. (2) Delete: DryRunEngine.SimulateAsync (:123-241), the nested ReportBuilder (:642-758), the constants MaxReportBytes (:57), MaxReportedFiles (:58) and the seams ReportByteBudget (:83), MaxBatchCandidates (:95); the SimulateAsync member from IDryRunEngine (:15); src/FileManager.Core/IPC/Handlers/DryRunHandler.cs entirely and its two Program.cs registrations; tests/FileManager.Core.Tests/IPC/Handlers/DryRunHandlerTests.cs; the SimulateAsync stub from the three fake engines in DryRunStreamHandlerTests.cs (:31, :163, :362); the DryRunRequest round-trip at tests/FileManager.Service.Tests/EndToEndSmokeTests.cs:187-188 (replace with the streamed request it already exercises); and benchmarks/FileManager.Core.Benchmarks/DryRun/DryRunEngineBenchmarks.cs:169 (retarget to SimulateStreamAsync).

Migration story for the frozen wire surface: do NOT touch Contracts. DryRunRequest, DryRunResponse and their "dry-run"/"dry-run-report" discriminators, IpcRequestTypes.DryRun and its DiscriminatorOf case, and the SerializationTests that pin them all stay exactly as they are — the wire vocabulary is unchanged and IpcRequestTypesTests still passes. Removing only the handler means the discriminator drops out of the dispatch dictionary and a sender would get NOT_IMPLEMENTED; since no protocol-6 client sends it (verified above), also bump IpcRequest.CurrentProtocolVersion 6 → 7 so any pre-streaming build fails loud with IPC_VERSION_MISMATCH instead, and record the removal in docs/specs/architecture-v1.md §8.

*Blast radius:* 11 files, 14 call sites.

src (5): DryRunEngine.cs, IDryRunEngine.cs, DryRunHandler.cs (delete), Program.cs (2 registration lines), IpcRequest.cs (version bump only). tests (5): DryRunEngineTests.cs (7 calls), DryRunPipelineTests.cs (6 calls), DryRunHandlerTests.cs (delete), DryRunStreamHandlerTests.cs (3 stubs), EndToEndSmokeTests.cs (1). benchmarks (1): DryRunEngineBenchmarks.cs. Contracts records and their SerializationTests are deliberately untouched.

*Prerequisites:* An explicit human decision that the batched/CLI dry-run is abandoned, recorded in docs/specs/architecture-v1.md; An explicit human decision that a protocol version bump 6→7 is wanted now; Step 1 (port all 12 SimulateAsync assertions to SimulateStreamAsync via the existing CollectStream helper) landed and green ON ITS OWN, before a single deletion

*Verify:* After step 1 alone, the ported tests must pass against the streamed path — that is the proof the streamed pipeline covers what the batched tests asserted. After deletion: tests/FileManager.Core.Tests/IPC/IpcRequestTypesTests.cs and tests/FileManager.Contracts.Tests/IPC/SerializationTests.cs must pass UNTOUCHED (proving the wire vocabulary did not move — Contracts is not edited), and EndToEndSmokeTests must still complete a dry run over the real pipe. A pre-streaming build must then fail loud with IPC_VERSION_MISMATCH rather than NOT_IMPLEMENTED.

## Findings detail

All 30 kept findings, each verified against the source. `verdict` records what the
adversarial verifier did to the finder's original severity claim.

### Severity: high (5)

#### `dryrun-tabs-one-class-written-twice` — DryRunSourcesTab and DryRunDestinationsTab are the same class written twice — the repo's hottest file, and fixes are being pasted into both halves

| | |
|---|---|
| Lens | god-components-srp |
| Severity | high (verifier verdict: downgrade) |
| Confidence | high |
| Effort | medium |
| Risk flags | perf-sensitive, wide-blast-radius, touches-generated-code |

**Claim.** DryRunSourcesTab (DryRunViewModel.cs:1160-1610, 451 lines) and DryRunDestinationsTab (DryRunViewModel.cs:1611-2110, 500 lines) declare the identical field set, the identical 14 observable properties, and the identical 13-method lifecycle (ComputeLoad/Load/Clear/BuildStatusFilters/SelectedStatusKeys/ClearStatusFilters/OnFacetChanged/OnStatusFilterChanged/RequestRebuild/RebuildAsync/ComputeRebuild/BuildTree). After normalizing only the row type name, a diff of the two regions shows 169 differing lines out of 951 — roughly 390 of 451 lines are byte-identical. There is no base class, no generic, and no shared helper. The variation is confined to six named things: the TreePillSpec list, the status-count vocabulary, the facet-key extraction, the sort-key extraction, the per-row filter predicate, and the tree-leaf projection.

**Evidence.**

- `src/FileManager.UI/ViewModels/DryRunViewModel.cs:1160`

  ```csharp

  {
      private static readonly IReadOnlyList<TreePillSpec> TreeSpecs = [...]

      private List<DryRunFileRow> _visible = [];
  ```

- `src/FileManager.UI/ViewModels/DryRunViewModel.cs:1611`

- `src/FileManager.UI/ViewModels/DryRunViewModel.cs:1201`

  ```csharp

  {
      // Dispose the previous grid source after the new value has propagated to the bound
      // TreeDataGrid. HierarchicalTreeDataGridSource owns a realized HierarchicalRows cache whose
      // per-row wrappers subscribe to each node's IsExpanded — never disposing it lets the control's
      // realization keep the whole old forest alive ...
  ```
